sources.entry: Site reliability engineering kicks rote tasks out of IT ops

summary.name: Site reliability engineering (SRE)
summary.one_liner: An explainer article describing site reliability engineering (SRE), the practice of applying scripting and automation to IT operations tasks like maintenance and support.
use_cases: understanding what an SRE team does
defining SLAs, SLOs and SLIs for a service
reviewing history of site reliability engineering
summary.what_it_does: The page is an overview article rather than a software tool. It defines site reliability engineering as applying scripting and automation to IT operations work such as maintenance and support, with the aim of fixing bugs quickly and removing manual rote tasks. It explains how SRE uses SLAs, SLOs, SLIs and error budgets to measure and maintain reliability. It contrasts SRE with DevOps, lists typical SRE qualifications, and gives a brief history starting with Google's 2003 team led by Benjamin Treynor Sloss.
notable: Compares SRE and DevOps roles and how they collaborate
Traces SRE origins to Google's 2003 team led by Benjamin Treynor Sloss
Lists typical SRE qualifications such as Linux, networking, scripting and cloud skills
caveats: Describes a practice and job role, not a downloadable tool or product
Small and medium organizations may find a dedicated SRE too costly, per the article
